gloss: to open up; to warm up to

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {打|う}ち{解|と}けていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to open up; to warm up to; to become friendly
definitions.explanation: to relax one's guard and become comfortable or friendly with someone

examples.english: He quickly warmed up to everyone.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{緊張|きんちょう}していた→緊張する：20557_kinchousuru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧うち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{打|う}ち{解|と}けた。
examples.english: I was nervous at first, but I opened up as we talked.

examples.japanese: {打|う}ち{解|と}けた⟦{雰囲気|ふんいき}→雰囲気：03604_funiki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{進|すす}んだ→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: The meeting proceeded in a relaxed atmosphere.

notes:
{打|う}ち{解|と}ける is a compound verb combining ⟦{打|う}つ→打つ：01221_utsu⟧ (to strike) + ⟦{解|と}ける→解ける：04371_tokeru⟧ (to loosen), expressing the breaking down of barriers between people.

VERB TYPE:
- Ichidan verb (る-verb)
- Intransitive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {打|う}ち{解|と}けた⟦{雰囲気|ふんいき}→雰囲気：03604_funiki⟧ (relaxed atmosphere)
- {打|う}ち{解|と}けた⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧ (friendly relationship)
- ⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{打|う}ち{解|と}ける (to quickly warm up)
- ⟦なかなか→なかなか：01547_nakanaka⟧{打|う}ち{解|と}けない (to not easily open up)
- ～⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{打|う}ち{解|と}ける (to warm up to ~)

USAGE:
- Often describes the process of becoming comfortable with new people
- The adjective form {打|う}ち{解|と}けた is commonly used to describe atmospheres and relationships
- Implies overcoming initial awkwardness or formality

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{親|した}しく→親しい：02345_shitashii⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become close)
- ⟦{仲良|なかよ}く→仲良い：29434_nakayoi⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (to become friendly)
- ⟦{心|こころ}→心：01321_kokoro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧ (to open one's heart)
- ⟦{氷|こおり}→氷：02753_koori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{解|と}ける→解ける：04371_tokeru⟧ (the ice breaks - idiom)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
